Optimal Enhancement Control of Static V oltage
Stability Margin for AC/DC Power System With
Renewables Considering Control Mode Switching of
DC Converter Stations
Wanbin Liu, Shunjiang Lin , Senior Member , IEEE, Y uerong Y ang , Student Member , IEEE, Ziqing Y ang ,
Mingbo Liu , Member , IEEE, and Qifeng Li , Senior Member , IEEE
Abstract—In an AC/DC power system with high penetration of
renewable energy stations (RESs), the injected bus power has high
random ﬂuctuation, which brings great challenges to ensuring the
sufﬁcient static voltage stability margin (SVSM) of the system. In
this paper, considering the impact of uncertain RES output and DC
converter stations’ control mode switching with the load growth,
an optimal SVSM enhancement control model for AC/DC power
system is proposed. In the model, the SVSM of the system under
uncertain RES power is enhanced by regulating the power output
and terminal voltage of generators and the parameters of multiple
control modes of DC converter stations. By proposing a triangular
convex hull relaxation method and using the uncertainty-aware
model (UaM) method and the Karush–Kuhn–Tucker condition
of inner-layer optimization model, the proposed bi-layer optimal
SVSM enhancement control model is transformed into a single-
layer nonlinear programming model, which can be directly solved
by the CONOPT solver with high efﬁciency. Case study on the mod-
iﬁed 39-bus AC/DC power system demonstrates that the obtained
SVSM enhancement control scheme can accurately consider the
inﬂuence of DC converter stations’ control mode switching with
the load growth, identify the inﬂuence of uncertain injected bus
power on the system SVSM, and enhance the SVSM to satisfy the
required secure operation level.
Index Terms —AC/DC power system, control mode switching,
improved relaxed LASSO, Karush–Kuhn–Tucker condition,
optimal enhancement control, static voltage stability margin.

I. I NTRODUCTION
S
TATIC voltage stability margin (SVSM) is a commonly
used index for reﬂecting the voltage stability degree of the
current operating point of a power system, which is useful for
guiding the secure operation of the power system [1].I ft h e
SVSM of a power system is small, voltage instability cases are
easy to occur with the load growth in the system operation, which
will result in the power outage of the system. There have been
some power outage accidents related to voltage instability in
actual power systems, such as the off-grid accident in Texas, the
United States of America in 2022, and the repeated crossing of
low voltage problems in the northern Hebei power grid of China
in 2021, and so on [2], [3]. Thus, to ensure the secure operation
of a power system, the SVSM is required to be maintained above
a given level, such as 0.15 in the Code on security and stability
for power system in China [4]. With the increasing penetration
of renewable energy generation into power systems, the impact
of uncertain power output of renewable energy stations (RESs)
on SVSM is becoming signiﬁcant [5], [6]. Meanwhile, with the
rapid increase of line-commutated converter-based high voltage
direct current (LCC-HVDC) and voltage source converter-based
high voltage direct current (VSC-HVDC) transmission lines in
power systems, they can increase the ﬂexible regulating ability of
the system to enhance the SVSM. Thus, how to coordinate vari-
ous regulation measures to enhance the SVSM of AC/DC power
system considering the uncertain RES power output poses great
challenge [7], [8]. The optimal SVSM enhancement control is
attributed to the optimal static voltage stability (SVS) control
problem, which is mainly divided into two categories[9].O n ei s
the control strategies of regulating the current operation point to
prevent voltage collapse at a future moment after load ﬂuctuation
or before an accident, which is called preventive SVS control
[10], [11]. The other is the control strategies to alleviate voltage
instability after the occurrence of a large disturbance in the power
system and a voltage collapse, called corrective SVS control
[12], [13]. The optimal SVSM enhancement control in this paper
belongs to the preventive SVS control. It aims to regulate the
current operation point to ensure that the SVSM meet the secure
operation requirements of the system considering the uncertain
RES output.

Nowadays, many scholars have studied the optimal preventive
SVS control problem. In [14], an optimal reactive power reserve
management scheme to improve the system SVS based on
optimal power ﬂow (OPF) model is proposed. Mahdavi et al.[15]
proposes a predictive SVS control method in a power distribution
system with high penetration of photovoltaic units to maintain
system voltages within an appropriate bandwidth. Hao et al.
[16] proposes a multi-contingency preventive control method for
SVS, and comprehensively considers the SVSM requirements
under multi-contingency. Wang et al.[17] proposes a preventive
control strategy based on efﬁcient power plant model of electric
vehicles to maintain the SVSM above a predeﬁned security
level. However, the above literatures do not take into account
the uncertainty of RES output. There are two main categories
to deal with the uncertain RES output in the optimal preventive
SVS control problem. One is to consider the uncertainty as a
whole in the control process, and the most conservative con-
trol strategy can be obtained. In [18], the uncertain ﬂuctuation
ranges of wind farm output are described as intervals, and a
multi-objective optimal SVS control model is proposed. In [19],
an optimal SVSM control model considering the uncertain wind
farm output is proposed, and a probabilistic distribution control
method is proposed to solve the optimal SVSM control model.
The other is to establish an online preventive control model to
ensure that the optimal control strategy can be updated during
the change of uncertain RES output. In[20], an online preventive
control optimization model for on-line voltage stability of large
power grids considering multiple critical emergencies is pro-
posed. However, when the penetration of renewable energy is
high, the system state varies frequently, and the required trigger
time of system regulation often leads to the failure of online
preventive control to meet the actual operation requirements.
Hence these two categories still have limitations in practical
applications under the high uncertainty environment. Thus, to
propose a new method to better accommodate the uncertainties
in optimal SVS control to obtain a more secure and accurate
control strategy is required.
In addition, different from pure AC power systems, more extra
DC control measures can be used in AC/DC power systems.
Hence the SVSM can also be enhanced by optimizing the control
modes and control parameters of DC converter stations. In
[21], a novel control algorithm for improving SVS by using
an embedded VSC-HVDC system is proposed. In [22], a coor-
dinate strategy of control modes of inverter and transformer is
proposed to improve the SVS of AC/DC systems. The above
research demonstrates that regulating the control performance
of LCC/VSC-HVDC is beneﬁcial to enhance the system SVSM.
Since SVSM is reﬂecting the maximum load growth that a power
system can bear in the current operating state. In actual situation,
with the load growth, the control modes of a DC converter station
may switch from one to another. If the DC converter stations’
control mode switching with the load growth is not considered,
the obtained SVSM of AC/DC power system will be inaccurate.
If the SVSM value is evaluated to be bigger than actual situation,
it will bring risks to the secure operation of the system. If the
SVSM value is evaluated to be smaller than actual situation, it
will bring extra control costs to the system operation. Thus, this
paper will study various control modes of DC converter stations
and their switching with the load growth, and take them into
account in the optimal SVSM enhancement control model of
AC / DC power system with renewables.
This paper makes two contributions. 1) A bi-level opti-
mization model for optimal SVSM enhancement control of
AC/DC power system with renewables is proposed, in which
the inner-layer SVSM calculation model includes the constraints
for describing the control mode switching of DC converter
stations with the load growth. It can reﬂect the impact of DC
converter stations’ control mode switching with the load growth
on the SVSM of AC/DC power system. 2) A triangle convex
hull relaxation method is proposed to convexify the nonlinear
control mode switching constraints of DC converter stations.
The improved relaxed least absolute shrinkage and selection
operator (IR-LASSO) regression based convex approximation
method is used to identify the approximately convex relation-
ship between the uncertain RES output and the bus voltage in
the extended power ﬂow equation (PFE) constraints. They can
improve the solution efﬁciency and reliability of the optimal
SVSM enhancement control model.
The rest of this paper is organized as follows. Section II
describes the optimal SVSM enhancement control model of
AC/DC power system with renewables. Section III introduces
the solution method of the optimal SVSM enhancement control
model. The case study and conclusions of the modiﬁed 39-bus
AC/DC hybrid power system are displayed in SectionsIV and V,
respectively.
II. O PTIMAL SVSM ENHANCEMENT CONTROL MODEL OF
AC/DC POWER SYSTEM WITH RENEW ABLES
The optimal SVSM enhancement control model of AC/DC
power system with renewables considering the control mode
switching of DC converter stations takes the generators’ active
power output and terminal voltage, and the control parameters
of DC converter stations’ control modes as the control variables.
Through the coordinate control of various control measures in
the AC/DC system, the system SVSM in ensured to meet the
given secure operation requirements. The model mainly includes
the objective function, the normal operation constraints of the
AC/DC power system with renewables, the control mode switch-
ing constraints of DC converter stations, and the inner-layer
SVSM calculation model constraint.

C. Inner-Layer SVSM Calculation Model Constraints
Considering DC Converter Stations’ Control Mode Switching
For the variable λm representing the system SVSM in the
constraint (10), it is necessary to establish an inner-layer SVSM
calculation model to solve it. DC converter stations have multiple
control modes, which can meet various operation requirement
of AC/DC hybrid power systems. With the load growth, the
control modes of a DC converter station may switch from one
to another, and this process is required to be considered in the
SVSM calculation model. Most existing publications about DC
converter stations’ control mode switching are as follows: in
each system operation state, all possible control modes are se-
lected and switched to the optimal control mode [23]. However,
this control logic is not in line with the actual situations. In
actual operation, a control mode cannot be switched to another
control mode arbitrary. Taking the switching between constant
DC voltage control and constant extinction angle control of the
inverter station of LCC-HVDC as an example, according to the
3rd equation in (8), with the load growth, in order to keep the DC
voltage UdIi unchanged, it is necessary to reduce the extinction
angle γi of the inverter station. In order to avoid the commu-
tation failure, γi has a lower limit. When γi reaches the lower
limit, the control mode of inverter station will be switched to
constant minimum extinction angle control. Thus, the control
mode switching of actual LCC and VSC converter stations has
several relatively ﬁxed switching processes.
References [24], [25] proposed that the control mode of a DC
converter station is switched according to a certain default order.
This method avoids the occurrence of unreasonable control
mode switching strategy. Therefore, assuming that the LCC- and
VSC- HVDC converter stations’ control modes switch according
to the default order. The default order of the control modes
of LCC-HVDC converter stations is expressed in the Ud-Id
coordinate system [24], as shown in Fig. 1. It can be seen that
according to the order of the increase of DC current Id,t h e
LCC-HVDC inverter side’s control modes are VDCOL control,
constant Id control at IdIref, constant Ud control, and constant
extinction angle control sequentially. The LCC-HVDC rectiﬁer
side’s control modes are VDCOL control, constant Id control,
and constant rectiﬁer’s delay trigger angle control.
It can be observed from Fig. 1 that the initial control mode of
the LCC-HVDC transmission system is constant Id control on
the rectiﬁer side and constant Ud control on the inverter side,
i.e., the intersection point of two broken lines of the rectiﬁer
and inverter stations. With the load growth, the control mode
of rectiﬁer side can be switched to VDCOL control or constant
rectiﬁer’s delay trigger angle control, and the control mode of
inverter side can be switched to constant DC current control or
constant extinction angle control. The control mode switching

III. S OLUTION METHODOLOGY
To solve the above bi-level optimization model, by using
the KKT condition, the inner-layer SVSM calculation model is
transformed into constraints, thereby transforming the bi-level
optimization model into a single-level optimization model [18].
In order to ensure that the solution obtained by the constraints
after KKT condition transformation is the optimal solution of
the original model, the nonlinear constraints in the inner-layer
SVSM calculation model are required to be convexiﬁed at ﬁrst.
Thus, the original bi-layer continuous non-convex optimization
model is transformed into a single-layer continuous optimization

interval result. In addition, the control cost of enhancing a SVSM
value to meet the secure operation requirements is often smaller

method to deal with the uncertain RES power and the convex

V. C ONCLUSION
In this study, an optimal SVSM enhancement control model
of AC/DC power system with RESs is proposed. In this model,
the control mode switching constraints of DC converter stations
described by multiple complementary equations are added. By
adjusting the generators’ initial active power output and terminal
voltage and the parameters of various control modes of DC
converter stations, the system SVSM under the uncertain RES
output is enhanced. By convex approximation of the extended
PFEs, and the triangular convex hull relaxation of the control
mode switching constraints of DC converter stations, the inner-
layer SVSM calculation model is transformed into its KKT con-
ditions, then the proposed bi-layer optimal SVSM enhancement
control model is transformed into a single-layer optimization
model for direct solution. Case study on the modiﬁed IEEE-39
bus system shows that the proposed convex approximation and
the triangular convex hull relaxation method have high com-
putational accuracy. The optimal control scheme obtained by
solving the proposed model can effectively enhance SVSM to
be bigger than the secure operation requirements. Taking the
control mode switching of the DC converter stations with the
load growth into account in the optimal SVSM enhancement
control is beneﬁcial to improve the SVSM of the AC/DC power
system.
The proposed method can be applied to guide the operation of
actual AC/DC power systems to execute the preventive control
measures to increase the SVSM of current operating point to
meet the secure operation requirements. The preventive control
measures include regulating the generators’ initial active power
output and terminal voltage and DC stations’ control mode
parameters. It can effectively avoid the occurrence of voltage
instability and power outage cases in the system operation.
This paper only focuses on the optimal SVSM enhancement
control problem under normal operation of an AC/DC power
system. However, the inﬂuence of DC converter stations’ control
mode switching on SVSM can also be considered in the optimal
SVSM enhancement control problem under multiple N-1 con-
tingencies. How to solve this problem is a possible direction of
future work.
